extra.message: Insecure Deserialization via pickle.loads on user input — Remote code execution; an attacker can execute arbitrary Python code on the server. [verified: Duplicate of finding 2/19: same `pickle.loads(raw)` on attacker-supplied bytes at line 68; no safe unpickling, arbitrary code execution via `__reduce__`.]

Path Traversal with Sensitive Data Write — Arbitrary directory write of JSON files containing PII (SSN, card numbers); overwrite existing files if parent directory traversal is used. [verified: Duplicate of finding 4/21: same `BASE_EXPORT_DIR / f"{ref}.json"` traversal at line 87; writes JSON with SSN/card data to attacker-controlled filesystem path.]

Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI) via Jinja2 — Remote code execution through Jinja2 template expression injection; full server compromise. [verified: Duplicate of finding 1/18: same `Template("Result: " + fragment).render()` SSTI via Jinja2 at line 145; attacker-controlled template string with no sandbox.]

Path Traversal to Arbitrary File Write — Arbitrary file write anywhere on the filesystem; possible RCE via cron job, SSH key, or code injection. [verified: Duplicate of finding 3/20: same path traversal via `BASE_EXPORT_DIR / name` at line 152 with `request.body` written to attacker-chosen path; no `Path.resolve()` or traversal check.]

Server-Side Template Injection (Jinja2) in acct_jinja_cast_488 — Arbitrary code execution on the server through Jinja2 template expression injection, enabling full system compromise. [verified: Duplicate of finding 1/18/33: same `Template("Result: " + fragment).render()` at line 145; Jinja2 template injection on attacker-controlled string with no sandbox or escaping.]

OS Command Injection via host parameter — Remote code execution on the server with the privileges of the Django process. [verified: Duplicate of finding 0/17: same `os.system("ping -c 1 " + host)` OS command injection at line 161; zero shell-escaping, `_wrk_gate` is authentication-only.]

Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI) in acct_jinja_cast_488 — Remote code execution via Jinja2 template injection. Attacker can execute arbitrary Python on the server, read sensitive files, access database, and pivot to internal infrastructure. [verified: `Template("Result: " + fragment).render()` at line 145 concatenates attacker-controlled GET param `fragment` directly into a Jinja2 Template string; Jinja2 Template() on untrusted input allows SSTI→RCE with no escaping or sandboxing.]

OS Command Injection in acct_shell_probe_506 — Remote code execution on the server with the privileges of the Django process, enabling full system compromise. [verified: Duplicate of finding 0/17/31: same `os.system("ping -c 1 " + host)` at line 161; zero sanitization, `_wrk_gate` is only auth, attacker-controlled host param allows arbitrary command injection.]

Path Traversal with Arbitrary File Write in acct_dock_shelf_494 — Arbitrary file write to any location writable by the Django process. Attacker can overwrite application code, upload webshells, modify configuration, or write cron jobs to achieve persistent access. [verified: `BASE_EXPORT_DIR / name` at line 152 uses attacker-controlled GET param `name` with no `Path.resolve()` check, `os.path.commonpath`, or traversal sanitization; `target.write_bytes(request.body)` writes attacker content to arbitrary filesystem locations.]

OS Command Injection in acct_shell_probe_506 — Remote code execution on the web server with the privileges of the Django process. Attacker can read files, exfiltrate database, pivot internally. [verified: `os.system("ping -c 1 " + host)` at line 161 concatenates attacker-controlled GET param `host` directly into shell command with zero sanitization, escaping, or shlex.quote(); `_wrk_gate` is only an authentication gate, not an input control.]

Hardcoded Django SECRET_KEY Fallback in settings.py — If deployed without setting DJANGO_SECRET_KEY, an attacker who knows the default key can forge session cookies (session hijacking), craft valid CSRF tokens (CSRF bypass), generate valid password reset tokens (account takeover), and tamper with any signed data. [verified: settings.py line 6: SECRET_KEY falls back to hardcoded 'dev-only-change-me' when DJANGO_SECRET_KEY env var is unset; no compensating control prevents use of this predictable key for cryptographic signing of sessions, CSRF tokens, and password reset tokens.]

Hardcoded Default SECRET_KEY — Session hijacking, CSRF token forgery, password reset token forgery, and general compromise of all Django cryptographic signing. [verified: Same hardcoded SECRET_KEY fallback to 'dev-only-change-me' at line 6; no compensating control neutralizes the predictable key when DJANGO_SECRET_KEY is unset.]

DEBUG=True by Default in settings.py — Detailed error pages expose application internals including secret keys, database credentials, file paths, SQL queries, and source code snippets. This enables attackers to understand application structure, discover additional vulnerabilities, and potentially extract credentials. [verified: settings.py line 7: DEBUG defaults to True when DJANGO_DEBUG env var is unset (os.getenv('DJANGO_DEBUG','1')=='1'); SecurityMiddleware is present but no SECURE_* settings are configured to suppress error page detail.]

Hardcoded Database Credentials in Settings and Docker Compose — Anyone with access to the source code or docker-compose.yml can obtain database credentials, enabling direct database access and data exfiltration. [verified: POSTGRES_PASSWORD defaults to 'crm_saas' at line 53 and docker-compose.yml embeds the same weak credential; no compensating network restriction or auth override prevents use of the default.]

IDOR: Support Agent Gains Full Org Access from Single Escalation Assignment — Support agents with a single escalation assignment can view all deals (with monetary values), internal documents, API keys, webhooks, and contacts across the entire organization, enabling horizontal privilege escalation and data exfiltration. [verified: can_access_org() at authz.py:28-29 grants SUPPORT_AGENT full org access if org.escalations.filter(assigned_agent=user).exists() — a single escalation assignment unlocks all deals (with values), all documents including internal, all API keys, and all webhooks via organization_detail. No additional scoping or filtering exists; the access check is binary and overly permissive.]

Hardcoded Demo Passwords in Seed Command — Unauthorized access to demo user accounts including platform_admin if seed command is run outside ephemeral environments. [verified: Module-level constant PASSWORD='DemoPass123!' at line 14 is used via user.set_password(PASSWORD) for all demo users including platform_admin; no env-guard (DEBUG check or similar) prevents the command from running in non-ephemeral environments, and the seed_demo management command is a listed CLI entry point.]

Hardcoded Default Password for Invited Customer Users — Any customer contact invited to the platform receives the same known password. An attacker who knows or discovers this password can access any invited customer's account, view their organization data, documents, escalations, and PII including contacts' names, emails, and phone numbers. [verified: Line 199 sets user.set_password('DemoPass123!') for every invited customer contact — all invited accounts share the same well-known password with no forced-reset mechanism, enabling unauthorized access to any invited user's organization data, PII, and escalations.]

Sensitive Credentials Written to Application Logs — Authorization tokens/credentials captured in log files accessible to anyone with log read access; credential leakage. [verified: Duplicate of finding 8/24: same `logger.warning()` at line 38 logging raw `Authorization` header and full request body as plaintext; credentials persisted in application logs.]

Open Redirect via lane Parameter — Phishing; attackers can craft URLs that redirect authenticated users to malicious external sites while appearing to originate from the trusted CRM domain. [verified: Duplicate of finding 5/23: same `redirect(next_url)` at line 45 with attacker-controlled `lane` param; no `is_safe_url()` or allow-list, enables phishing redirects.]

Sensitive Data in Logs via account_casefeed_roll_032 — Leakage of bearer tokens, API keys, or PII from request bodies into persistent log files accessible to operators and potentially log aggregation systems. [verified: Duplicate of finding 8: same `logger.warning()` at line 38 logging raw Authorization header and request body in plaintext with no redaction or masking.]

Business Logic Bypass (Negative Amount) and Mass Assignment of State in acct_delta_127 — Attacker can arbitrarily inflate the ledger balance via negative amount and set state to any value, bypassing business rules. [verified: No sign validation on amount allows negative values to inflate balance via ledger['balance'] -= amount; state is mass-assignable from user-controlled payload. Impact confined to in-memory ledger response dict with no persistent state change.]

Sensitive PII Written to Disk in Plaintext — PII (SSN, credit card numbers) stored in plaintext on the filesystem; accessible to anyone with filesystem read access or through path traversal. [verified: Lines 88-90 write attacker-supplied `ssn` and `card` GET params directly to a plaintext JSON file on disk via `json.dumps()` and `write_text()`; PII stored unencrypted on filesystem with no protection, gated by `_wrk_gate`.]

Mass Assignment via workset.update() in acct_workset_rebind_197 — Attacker can escalate role to admin, set approved=true, and manipulate balance to arbitrary values by sending crafted JSON/POST body. [verified: No field allowlist or validation on payload before workset.update(payload); attacker-supplied keys like role, tier, approved, and balance overwrite defaults. Impact confined to in-memory response dict with no persistent state change.]

Sensitive PII (SSN/Credit Card) Written to Disk in Plaintext — Social Security numbers and credit card numbers are stored unencrypted on disk, violating PCI-DSS and data protection requirements; accessible to anyone with filesystem access. [verified: Duplicate of finding 38: same `acct_vault_stash_239` writing attacker-supplied SSN/card values to plaintext JSON at lines 88-90; PII persisted unencrypted on disk with no protection.]

Missing Authentication on Ops Endpoint — Anonymous access to an internal partner console endpoint; can submit arbitrary operational data. [verified: Duplicate of finding 6/22: `acct_identity_ping_337` at line 100-103 lacks `_wrk_gate()`; genuinely unauthenticated while all other 18 partner console endpoints require the token header.]

Permissive CORS with Credentials Reflection — Any external website can make authenticated cross-origin requests to this endpoint with the victim's cookies/session, leading to data theft or CSRF-like attacks. [verified: Duplicate of finding 7/25: same credentialed CORS wildcard via `Origin` header reflection at lines 123-124; any origin can make credentialed cross-origin requests.]

CORS Misconfiguration: Credentialed Wildcard via Origin Reflection — Any external website can make authenticated requests to the CRM on behalf of logged-in users, enabling CSRF-like attacks and data theft across origins. [verified: Duplicate of finding 7/25/37: same `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` mirroring with `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true` at lines 123-124; credentialed CORS from any origin.]

Missing Secure Cookie Flags — Session cookies transmitted over cleartext HTTP; session hijacking via network sniffing. [verified: No SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE or CSRF_COOKIE_SECURE in settings.py; Django defaults Secure to False, leaving cookies exposed over unencrypted HTTP.]

Missing Production Security Headers and TLS Configuration — No HTTPS enforcement, missing HSTS, cookies transmitted over cleartext HTTP, no X-Content-Type-Options or X-XSS-Protection headers in production. [verified: settings.py configures none of SECURE_HSTS_SECONDS, SECURE_SSL_REDIRECT, SECURE_BROWSER_XSS_FILTER, SECURE_CONTENT_TYPE_NOSNIFF, or cookie Secure flags; SecurityMiddleware is in MIDDLEWARE but has no settings to activate these protections.]

Missing Secure Cookie Flags (HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite) — Session cookies transmitted in cleartext over HTTP can be intercepted via MITM attacks, enabling session hijacking. Missing SameSite increases CSRF risk. [verified: Secure cookie flags are unset (SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE/CSRF_COOKIE_SECURE default False); SESSION_COOKIE_HTTPONLY=True and SESSION_COOKIE_SAMESITE='Lax' are Django defaults that partially mitigate the HttpOnly/SameSite sub-claims, but the absent Secure flags and CSRF_COOKIE_HTTPONLY=False remain real vulnerabilities.]

Missing Secure Cookie Flags for Session and CSRF Cookies — Session cookies and CSRF tokens transmitted over HTTP (non-HTTPS) can be intercepted via network sniffing. CSRF tokens accessible to JavaScript can be stolen via XSS. In a production deployment, this weakens the entire authentication and CSRF protection system. [verified: settings.py contains no SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE or CSRF_COOKIE_SECURE configuration; Django defaults both to False, transmitting session/CSRF cookies over cleartext HTTP with no compensating HTTPS enforcement.]

Disabled Accounts Can Still Access Dashboard and Profile — Disabled users retain access to dashboard, profile editing, and organization listing despite being marked disabled. [verified: ensure_enabled() exists in authz.py but is only called inside can_access_org() (line 28) and the role_required decorator (line 75). Views like dashboard, profile, and organization_list are protected only by @login_required with no ensure_enabled call, no middleware, and no custom auth backend checking profile.disabled. A disabled user with an active session can access these views.]

Unrestricted File Upload Without Content Validation — Uploaded malicious HTML/SVG files can execute JavaScript in victims' browsers when accessed via the media URL; potential stored XSS. [verified: DocumentForm (line 61) delegates to clean_file() which validates only size, not content; the media URL path bypasses the as_attachment=True FileResponse in document_download, so HTML uploads execute in-browser with app-origin privileges when DEBUG=True (the default).]

Webhook Secrets Stored in Plaintext — Database compromise exposes all webhook signing secrets, enabling forged webhook deliveries. [verified: The full secret string (ApiKey.make_secret()[0][:40]) is assigned to Webhook.secret on line 192/193 and persisted as-is; the field has no encryption or hashing, and the ApiKey model's hash-only pattern is a direct contrast showing the control is missing.]

Webhook Secrets Stored in Plaintext — Database compromise reveals all webhook HMAC secrets, allowing attackers to forge webhook deliveries to downstream systems. [verified: Same plaintext storage on line 192 — Webhook.secret is generated via ApiKey.make_secret()[0][:40] and saved verbatim in views.py:432 with no hashing step, unlike ApiKey which stores secret_hash only.]

Webhook Secrets Stored in Plaintext in Database — Database compromise exposes all webhook secrets in plaintext. Attackers can use these secrets to forge webhook payloads, impersonate the CRM to third-party integrations, and potentially gain access to connected services that trust webhook signatures. [verified: Webhook.secret (line 192) is a plain CharField with no hashing; the ApiKey model just above (line 182-184) demonstrates the expected pattern of storing only a SHA-256 hash, but webhook secrets are stored raw — any DB compromise exposes them directly.]

Disabled User Bypass: Dashboard and List Views Missing Disabled Check — Users flagged as disabled retain access to dashboards, organization lists, escalation queues, reports, and CSV exports, leaking aggregate business data despite being administratively deactivated. [verified: dashboard (line 60), organization_list, escalation_queue, reports, and export_csv use only @login_required without calling ensure_enabled(); that check exists only inside can_access_org() and role_required(), neither of which gate these aggregate views, so a disabled user retains access to cross-org aggregate dashboards, reports, and CSV exports.]

Disabled User Can Edit Organizations via can_manage_org Without ensure_enabled — A disabled account can modify organization data (name, plan, status, health, owner, etc.) despite being marked disabled. [verified: can_manage_org (authz.py:34-35) checks only role and ownership, never calls ensure_enabled; no middleware or other layer blocks disabled users before organization_edit (views.py:149).]

Hardcoded Demo Password in Source Code and User Messages — All seeded demo accounts share a known default password; the password is broadcast to users in plaintext UI messages, enabling unauthorized access to demo or invite-created accounts. [verified: The claimed line 155 is inside organization_edit, not contact_invite, but the hardcoded DemoPass123! password IS set at line 199 and displayed at line 206 in contact_invite, and seed_demo.py line 15 creates all demo users with the same password — the vulnerability is real in this file.]

API Key Secret Exposed in Session-Backed Messages — The one-time API key secret persists in the session storage and HTML responses, enabling retrieval by anyone with session access, log access, or through browser history/caching. [verified: The claimed line 252 is in deal_delete (Deal deleted message), not api_key_create, but the identical messages.success() secret exposure exists at line 390 in api_key_create — the raw credential is echoed into session-backed messages with no consumption guard.]

Disabled User Can Edit Escalations via can_access_escalation Without ensure_enabled — A disabled account can edit escalation severity, status, assigned agent, internal notes, and customer summary. [verified: can_access_escalation (authz.py:40-47) checks role and ownership but lacks ensure_enabled; escalation_edit (views.py:281) gates solely on this helper with no compensating disabled check.]

Missing Disabled-User Check on escalation_queue View — A disabled user can still view and filter the escalation queue, leaking operational data across organizations. [verified: escalation_queue (views.py:302) relies on @login_required and visible_orgs, neither of which invoke ensure_enabled; no disabled screening exists on this read path.]

CSV Formula Injection in Export Endpoints — When exported CSV files are opened in spreadsheet applications, injected formulas can execute commands on the analyst's machine or exfiltrate data from the spreadsheet. [verified: The claimed line 306 is in escalation_queue, not export_csv, but the same unsanitized csv.writer.writerow() pattern at lines 476-486 writes user-controlled org.name and deal.name to CSV without formula injection mitigation — no form validation or output sanitization exists.]

Disabled User Can View and Modify Escalation Details via can_access_escalation Without ensure_enabled — A disabled account can view escalation data, change escalation status, and post comments — state-changing operations that should be blocked for disabled users. [verified: escalation_detail (views.py:315) gates on can_access_escalation which omits ensure_enabled; the view handles POST status transitions and comments without any disabled-user guard.]

API Key Secret Exposed in User-Facing Messages — API key secrets exposed in browser page source, session storage, and proxy logs; anyone who can view the admin's screen or intercept the HTTP response can steal the key. [verified: The claimed line 340 is in escalation_detail (comment.save), not API key exposure, but the identical vulnerability pattern exists at api_key_create line 390 — the raw API key secret is placed in messages.success() and persisted in the session/HTML.]

API Key One-Time Secret Exposed in HTTP Response and Session — The API key secret, intended as a one-time display, is transmitted in HTTP response body, stored in the Django messages session cookie, and potentially cached by browsers and proxies. An attacker who intercepts the response, reads browser cache, or leverages XSS can steal the API key. [verified: Line 390 in api_key_create writes the raw 43-character API key secret into messages.success(), which Django stores in the session backend and renders in the HTML response. No sanitization or one-time-only consumption mechanism exists; the secret persists in session until the messages queue is drained.]

CSV Formula Injection in Data Exports — When an admin opens the exported CSV in Excel, injected formulas can execute arbitrary system commands or exfiltrate data. [verified: Same export_csv function at lines 470-490 writes unsanitized user-controlled Organization.name, Deal.name, and Escalation.title to CSV; no formula injection mitigation exists on any export kind (renewals, health, escalations).]

Missing Disabled-User Check on reports View — A disabled user can access the reports dashboard showing at-risk organizations, pending renewals, and escalation statistics. [verified: reports (views.py:456) uses @login_required and visible_orgs with a CUSTOMER_CONTACT block but no ensure_enabled call; disabled staff-role users remain unfiltered.]

Missing Disabled-User Check on export_csv View — A disabled user can export sensitive CRM data (renewals, health scores, escalations) to CSV files. [verified: export_csv (views.py:468) depends on @login_required, a CUSTOMER_CONTACT guard, and visible_orgs — none check disabled status; disabled accounts can export CRM data.]

CSV Formula Injection in Export Functions — An attacker who can create or edit organizations/deals with names starting with formula characters (e.g., `=cmd|' /C calc'!A0`) can inject formulas into exported CSV files. When a victim opens the CSV in a spreadsheet application, the formula executes, enabling command execution or data exfiltration. [verified: Line 476-486 in export_csv writes user-controlled org.name and deal.name directly into CSV cells via csv.writer with no formula-character prefix/sanitization; OrganizationForm and DealForm impose no validation against =, @, +, or - leading characters, so an org name like '=cmd|'/C calc'!A0' will execute when the CSV is opened in a spreadsheet.]

CSV Formula Injection in CSV Export — Arbitrary command execution on the machine of any user who opens the exported CSV in Excel/LibreOffice with DDE enabled. [verified: Same code path as finding 2 — export_csv at line 476-486 writes unsanitized user-controlled field values to CSV with csv.writer; no single-quote prefix or formula-character stripping is applied to any exported column.]

Internal Filesystem Path Leaked in Error Response — Attackers learn the absolute server filesystem path, aiding path traversal and other filesystem-based attacks. [verified: Duplicate of finding 16/30/42: same `RuntimeError` at line 33 embedding `BASE_EXPORT_DIR` path, returned verbatim in JSON response at line 35; filesystem path disclosure gated by `_wrk_gate`.]

Internal Path Disclosure (BASE_EXPORT_DIR) in Error Response in account_memo_ping_031 — An attacker learns the full filesystem path of the private_exports directory, which is the same directory targeted by path traversal vulnerabilities (acct_dock_shelf_494, acct_vault_stash_239). This provides exact path information for exploitation. [verified: Line 33 raises `RuntimeError(f"failed to import {requested} from {BASE_EXPORT_DIR}")` and returns the message verbatim at line 35; leaks full `BASE_EXPORT_DIR` filesystem path to authenticated callers, gated by `_wrk_gate`.]

Error Information Leakage in account_memo_ping_031 — Internal exception class names exposed to attackers, helping map the codebase internals and identify vulnerable dependencies. [verified: Line 35 returns `exc.__class__.__name__` (e.g., 'RuntimeError') in JSON response body; leaks Python exception class name to callers but no stack traces or sensitive data beyond the class name, gated by `_wrk_gate`.]

Use of Cryptographically Broken MD5 Hash in acct_digest_fold_277 — MD5 is broken for integrity and collision resistance. While this endpoint only provides a hashing oracle, the use of MD5 indicates cryptographic weakness in the codebase that may extend to other uses. Collision attacks enable signature forgery if MD5 is used for verification. [verified: `hashlib.md5(phrase.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()` at line 97 uses cryptographically broken MD5; serves only as a hashing oracle with no downstream verification, but normalizes broken crypto in the codebase, gated by `_wrk_gate`.]

MD5 Hash Used for Digest Endpoint — Provides an MD5 hashing oracle; broken cryptographic primitive in use. [verified: Duplicate of finding 11/26: same `hashlib.md5()` at line 97; cryptographically broken hash with no security downstream dependency, gated by `_wrk_gate`.]

User/Account Enumeration via Differential HTTP Responses in acct_identity_hint_456 — An attacker can enumerate which handles exist by observing the difference between 404 and 403 responses. Once a valid handle is identified, the attacker can brute-force the 4-digit numeric verifier (only 10,000 possibilities), which is trivial given no rate limiting. [verified: Lines 115-118 return 404 for unknown handles vs 403 for known handles with wrong verifier; the differential HTTP status enables enumeration of valid handles (`north`/`south`), though gated by `_wrk_gate` and hardcoded to only two values.]

Security Headers Explicitly Disabled — Browser XSS protection and CSP are disabled; if this pattern is reused on HTML-rendering endpoints, XSS attacks become more effective. [verified: Duplicate of finding 13/29: same `X-XSS-Protection: 0` and empty CSP at lines 131-132; defense-in-depth headers disabled on JSON endpoint, gated by `_wrk_gate`.]

Hardcoded Verifier Secrets in acct_identity_hint_456 — Trivial brute-force of 4-digit numeric verifier codes; anyone with source code access can authenticate to this endpoint. [verified: Lines 112-113 hardcode verifier PINs `"4812"` and `"5930"` as 4-digit numeric secrets in source code; trivially brute-forced (10K combinations) with no account lockout, but endpoint is gated by `_wrk_gate`.]

Security Headers Disabled: X-XSS-Protection and CSP Set to Insecure Values — Browser XSS protections are disabled, and Content Security Policy is cleared, removing layers of defense against injected scripts on pages served by this endpoint. [verified: Duplicate of finding 13/29/47: same `X-XSS-Protection: 0` and empty CSP at lines 131-132; JSON-only endpoint so practical XSS defense impact is negligible, gated by `_wrk_gate`.]

Disabled XSS Protection and Empty Content-Security-Policy in acct_frame_slip_476 — Browsers will not apply XSS filtering or CSP restrictions to this response. While this endpoint returns static JSON, the removal of defense-in-depth headers on any endpoint indicates a security posture weakness. Combined with other vulnerabilities (SSTI, XSS), this increases exploitability. [verified: Lines 131-132 explicitly set `X-XSS-Protection: 0` and empty `Content-Security-Policy`; endpoint returns JSON not HTML, so defense-in-depth impact is minimal, but the headers are genuinely disabled, gated by `_wrk_gate`.]

Weak PRNG Used for Token Generation — Predictable tokens if used for security-sensitive purposes; an attacker can forecast future generated values. [verified: Duplicate of finding 10: same `random.choice()` at line 172 using Mersenne Twister instead of `secrets`; predictable PRNG for token generation, gated by `_wrk_gate`.]

Authorization Based on Client-Controlled Cookie/Header — An attacker can trivially escalate their privilege level to 'elevated' by setting a cookie or header value; downstream consumers of this response may grant unauthorized access. [verified: Duplicate of finding 14: same client-supplied `ops_badge` cookie/header at line 178 granting cosmetic `lane: elevated`; no actual privilege enforcement, gated by `_wrk_gate`.]

Weak PRNG (random.choice) Used for Token Generation — Predictable tokens enable attackers to forge or guess security tokens if they observe sufficient output from the PRNG. [verified: Duplicate of finding 10/43: same `random.choice()` Mersenne Twister at line 172 for token generation; non-cryptographic PRNG, predictable after sufficient output observation.]

Information Disclosure of Environment Variable and Filesystem Path — Reveals internal filesystem layout and configuration module name, aiding further targeted attacks. [verified: Duplicate of finding 15: same `acct_trace_panel_536` at line 187 exposing `DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE` and `BASE_EXPORT_DIR` in JSON response; internal path disclosure gated by `_wrk_gate`.]

TLS Certificate Verification Disabled — If the hardcoded URL is changed to a real hostname, all HTTPS traffic would be vulnerable to man-in-the-middle interception. [verified: Duplicate of finding 12/28: same `ssl._create_unverified_context()` at line 194; TLS verification disabled but hardcoded to `partner.invalid` which does not resolve, gated by `_wrk_gate`.]

Cryptographically Weak PRNG (random.choice) for Token Generation in acct_nonce_roll_516 — Tokens generated with Mersenne Twister can be predicted by an attacker who observes multiple outputs. If these tokens are used for any security-sensitive purpose (session tokens, password reset, API keys), they could be predicted and forged. [verified: `random.choice(alphabet)` at line 172 uses Mersenne Twister PRNG instead of `secrets` module; tokens are predictable after ~624 observations, though no downstream security use of generated tokens exists in the codebase and endpoint is gated by `_wrk_gate`.]

Client-Side Authorization via Cookie/Header in acct_badge_gate_526 — Any client can set the `ops_badge` cookie or `x-ops-badge` header to "lead" and receive elevated authorization response. While this endpoint's response is cosmetic (no actual privilege enforcement shown), the pattern of trusting client-supplied values for authorization is fundamentally broken and would be catastrophic if replicated elsewhere. [verified: Line 178 reads `ops_badge` cookie or `x-ops-badge` header entirely from client; if value is `"lead"` it returns `lane: elevated`, but the response is cosmetic with no actual privilege enforcement downstream, gated by `_wrk_gate`.]

Internal Path Disclosure (DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE and BASE_EXPORT_DIR) in acct_trace_panel_536 — An attacker learns the exact filesystem path of the application and the Django settings module name, aiding in path traversal attacks and targeted exploits. Combined with path traversal findings, this provides the exact paths needed for file overwrite attacks. [verified: Line 187 returns `os.environ.get("DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE")` and `str(BASE_EXPORT_DIR)` in JSON response body; leaks internal filesystem path and settings module name to authenticated partner console callers, gated by `_wrk_gate`.]

Disabled TLS Certificate Verification in acct_trust_drift_546 — If the hardcoded URL were changed to a user-controlled value or the partner.invalid domain were compromised, an attacker could perform MITM attacks to intercept and modify data in transit. The use of private SSL API underscores insecure patterns. [verified: `ssl._create_unverified_context()` at line 194 disables TLS certificate verification for the outbound HTTPS request; URL is hardcoded to non-resolving `partner.invalid`, limiting immediate impact, but the pattern is present and gated by `_wrk_gate`.]
